slides.title:
American kids 9–17
already use AI.
slides.body: Almost half have never talked about it with a parent.
slides.source: Common Sense Media, AI Census of tweens and teens, 2026

slides.title: Which AI have you tried?
slides.body: No judgment. You're mapping the territory, not catching them out.

slides.title: What did you make with it?
slides.body: Making something and copying an answer are very different things. Find out which one it was.

slides.title: Has it ever been wrong?
slides.body: Kids who have caught AI making a mistake learn to trust it the right amount.

slides.title: What would you never tell it?
slides.body: Full name, school, address, photos of friends. If they don't know the list yet, now they do.

slides.title: What should we make together?
slides.body: The easiest way to stay in the loop is to sit in it. Pick a weekend project.

slides.title:
Save this for
**dinner tonight**.
slides.body: And send it to the other grown-up in the house.
